content: 1. J.B.W. and colleagues validated the PHQ-9 as a concise measure for assessing the severity of depression. This study was published in the Journal of General Internal Medicine in 2001, highlighting its clinical utility. 2. Tol W.A., Leku M.R., Lakin D.P., Carswell K., Augustinavicius J., Adaku A., and others conducted a cluster randomized trial to evaluate guided self-help interventions aimed at reducing psychological distress among South Sudanese female refugees in Uganda. Their findings were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2020. 3. Epping-Jordan J.E., Harris R., Brown F.L., Carswell K., Foley C., García-Moreno C., and colleagues introduced Self-Help Plus (SH+), a novel stress management package developed by the World Health Organization (WHO). This was detailed in the journal World Psychiatry in 2016. 4. Warth M., Kessler J., Koehler F., Aguilar-Raab C., Bardenheuer H.J., and Ditzen B. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrating that brief psychosocial interventions significantly improve the quality of life for patients receiving palliative care. Their work was published in Palliative Medicine in 2019. 5. The WHO updated its Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) guidelines in 2015 to address mental, neurological, and substance use disorders, providing a comprehensive framework for global mental health care. 6. Moodley N., Saimen A., Zakhura N., Motau D., Setswe G., Charalambous S., and others explored the barriers to tuberculosis (TB) treatment adherence in South Africa, emphasizing the role of patient education and patient-centered approaches. Their study appeared in BMC Public Health in 2020. 7. Spitzer R.L., Kroenke K., Williams J.B.W., and Löwe B. developed the GAD-7, a brief tool for assessing generalized anxiety disorder. This was published in the Archives of Internal Medicine in 2006. 8. The WHO released an operational handbook on tuberculosis in 2022, focusing on drug-resistant TB treatment and providing updated clinical guidance. 9. The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) published clinical guidelines for managing generalized anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults, offering evidence-based recommendations. 10. Hayward S.E., Deal A., Rustage K., Nellums L.B., Sweetland A.C., Boccia D., and colleagues conducted a systematic review examining the relationship between mental health and the risk of active tuberculosis. Their findings were published in BMJ Open in 2022. 11. Rehm J., Samokhvalov A.V., Neuman M.G., Room R., Parry C., Lönnroth K., and others reviewed the association between alcohol use, alcohol use disorders, and tuberculosis, highlighting the public health implications. This study was published in BMC Public Health in 2009. 12. Imtiaz S., Shield K.D., Roerecke M., Samokhvalov A.V., Lönnroth K., and Rehm J. conducted meta-analyses to establish alcohol consumption as a significant risk factor for tuberculosis. Their work appeared in the European Respiratory Journal in 2017. 13. Deiss R.G., Rodwell T.C., and Garfein R.S. reviewed the intersection of tuberculosis and illicit drug use, providing updated insights in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2009. 14. The WHO's 2018 Global Status Report on Alcohol and Health provided a comprehensive overview of alcohol-related health issues and their global impact. 15. The 2017 World Drug Report by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) offered critical insights into global drug trends and their health implications. 16. Grenfell P., Baptista Leite R., Garfein R., De Lussigny S., Platt L., and Rhodes T. reviewed the literature on tuberculosis, injecting drug use, and integrated HIV-TB care, emphasizing the need for comprehensive interventions. This was published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence in 2013. 17. Raviglione M. and Poznyak V.T. called for action to address harmful alcohol use as a strategy for tuberculosis prevention and treatment. Their commentary appeared in the European Respiratory Journal in 2017. 18. Mlunde L.B., Sunguy B.F., Mbwambo J.K.K., Ubuguyu O.S., Yasuo J., and Jimba M. systematically reviewed the association between opioid agonist therapy and the initiation of antiretroviral therapy, highlighting its benefits. This was published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2016. 19. Nosyk B., Min J.E., Colley G., Lima V.D., Yip B., Milloy M.J., and others demonstrated the causal effect of opioid substitution treatment on adherence to HAART medication refills. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2015. 20. Morozova O., Dvoryak S., and Altice F.L. showed that methadone treatment improves tuberculosis treatment outcomes among hospitalized opioid-dependent patients in Ukraine. This study appeared in the International Journal of Drug Policy in 2013. 21. Batki S.L., Gruber V.A., Bradley J.M., Bradley M., and Delucchi K. conducted a controlled trial combining methadone treatment with directly observed isoniazid therapy for tuberculosis prevention in injection drug users. Their findings were published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence in 2002. 22. Babor T.F., Higgins-Biddle J.C., Saunders J.B., and Monteiro M.G. developed the AUDIT (Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test) guidelines for use in primary care, providing a practical tool for early detection. 23. The WHO's 2019 report on global suicide rates provided critical health estimates and emphasized the need for targeted prevention strategies. 24. The WHO's LIVE LIFE guide offers a comprehensive framework for implementing suicide prevention strategies at the national level. 25. Thornicroft G., Sunkel C., Aliev A.A., Baker S., Brohan E., El Chammay R., and others published a landmark report in The Lancet, addressing stigma and discrimination in mental health and calling for systemic change. 26. Candy B., Jones L., Drake R., Leurent B., and King M. reviewed interventions supporting informal caregivers of terminally ill patients, providing evidence-based recommendations in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 27. Lee J.Y., Kwon N., Goo G.Y., and Cho S.I. systematically reviewed the link between inadequate housing and pulmonary tuberculosis, highlighting the social determinants of health. Their study was published in BMC Public Health in 2022. 28. Gutwinski S., Schreiter S., Deutscher K., and Fazel S. updated the prevalence of mental disorders among homeless populations in high-income countries through a systematic review and meta-regression analysis. Their findings were published in PLoS Medicine in 2021. 29. Jarde A., Romano E., Afaq S., Elsony A., Lin Y., Huque R., and others conducted a meta-review on tuberculosis multimorbidity in lowand middle-income countries, emphasizing the need for integrated care. This was published in BMJ Open in 2022. 30. Jarde A., Ma R., Todowede O.O., Latif A., Yaqoob A., Afaq S., and others explored the prevalence and burden of complex tuberculosis multimorbidity in lowand middle-income countries through a systematic review and meta-analysis (unpublished, 2022). 31. The WHO's operational handbook on tuberculosis, Module 6, addresses the intersection of tuberculosis and mental health conditions, providing guidance for integrated care. 32. The WHO's guidelines for managing physical health conditions in adults with severe mental disorders emphasize the importance of holistic care approaches. 33. The WHO's Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) provides a framework for addressing mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in resource-limited settings. 34. The WHO's Building Back Better initiative focuses on sustainable mental health care systems following emergencies, emphasizing resilience and recovery. 35. The WHO's Psychological First Aid guide offers practical strategies for field workers to address mental health needs in crisis situations. 36. The WHO's toolkit for assessing mental health and psychosocial needs in humanitarian settings provides a structured approach for health actors in emergencies.
